questions.subject: Physics
questions.category: Kinetic Theory of Gases :: Multi-Concept Physical Modeling (Type 2)
questions.question: A container in [Kinetic Theory of Gases] holds a mixture of $1\text{ mole}$ of Helium (monoatomic, $C_v = \frac{3}{2}R$) and $2\text{ moles}$ of Hydrogen (diatomic, $C_v = \frac{5}{2}R$). What is the effective molar heat capacity at constant volume $C_{v,\text{mix}}$ of the mixture?
questions.solution: By thermal equipartition, $C_{v,\text{mix}} = \frac{n_1 C_{v1} + n_2 C_{v2}}{n_1 + n_2} = \frac{1(\frac{3}{2}R) + 2(\frac{5}{2}R)}{1 + 2} = \frac{13}{6} R$.
questions.explanation: Analyze the physical model and equations in Kinetic Theory of Gases.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.category: Kinetic Theory of Gases :: Numerical Derivation
questions.question: One mole of ideal gas undergoes a polytropic expansion $P V^2 = C$ in [Kinetic Theory of Gases] from volume $V_0 = 1\text{ m}^3$ at pressure $P_0 = 10^5\text{ Pa}$ to $V_1 = 2\text{ m}^3$. Calculate the magnitude of work done by the gas in $\text{kJ}$ rounded to nearest integer.
questions.solution: Work done in polytropic process with $n=2$: $W = \frac{P_0 V_0 - P_1 V_1}{n - 1} = P_0 V_0 \left(1 - \frac{V_0}{V_1}\right) = 10^5 \times 1 \times (1 - 0.5) = 5 \times 10^4\text{ J} = 50\text{ kJ}$.
questions.explanation: Calculate using quantitative physical laws in Kinetic Theory of Gases.
